title: Structural Resilience and Allosteric Rewiring: A Generative Blueprint for Overcoming Mutational Vulnerability in Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors
content: Traditional acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors often rely on static steric blockade, rendering them vulnerable to therapeutic stagnation and target-site mutations. This study developed a generative-to-kinetic screening pipeline to identify structurally resilient neurotherapeutics capable of overcoming mutational anchors. A virtual library of 100,000 compounds generated via the DrugEx framework was filtered using an empirically calibrated Jaccard applicability domain threshold of 0.823 to mitigate reward-hacking. Refined candidates underwent multi-parameter ADMET/CNS filtering and Butina clustering (Tanimoto ≥ 0.85), yielding 517 unique chemotypes. Following ensemble docking, four topographical probes were subjected to 100 ns molecular dynamics trajectories. Lead 1631, featuring a symmetrical bridging architecture, advanced to triplicate MD runs, Metadynamics, and Dynamic Cross-Correlation Matrix (DCCM) analysis. Non-canonical leads suffered catastrophic unbinding upon catalytic anchor loss, but the symmetrical Lead 1631 demonstrated profound resilience. Mutational stress induced a thermodynamic locking effect; the W86A mutant possessed a deeper energy well (9.23 ± 1.98 kJ/mol) than the wild-type (5.26 ± 1.69 kJ/mol). DCCM analysis quantified a mechanical inversion of the CAS-PAS axis, shifting from synchronized motion to an anti-correlated clamping mode (-0.04) that stabilizes the ligand. These results provide a robust computational blueprint for engineering neurotherapeutics, proving that mutational stress can be thermodynamically exploited via allosteric rewiring to maintain target stability.
